text:
Evidence supports candidate-distribution audits as diagnostics, without establishing that training-set stress results predict validation gains. [Krichene and Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/) show sampled candidates can reverse model comparisons even in expectation. Thus uniform versus popularity-weighted negatives can reveal candidate sensitivity; strong ranks on fitted training targets remain compatible with memorization. [Owen](https://arxiv.org/abs/0712.1111) shows naive bootstrap uncertainty can mislead with dependent recommender observations.

Proposed bounded protocol: freeze training-only user-prefix/next-item probes, excluding future interactions from each prefix. Prespecify three candidate conditions: 99 unique uniform negatives, 99 unique training-popularity-weighted negatives, and full-catalog ranking. Exclude known positives from negative pools; freeze seeds and sampling rules. Cap probes at 200 users/category and five prefixes/user. Report paired rank/margin changes and 95% intervals from 1,000 user-cluster bootstrap replicates, retaining all prefixes and candidate draws within each resampled user. Interpret intervals conditional on fitted checkpoints and catalog; they omit training-seed and item-population uncertainty. Before interpreting results, require generated working/predict.py and in-memory scores to agree within a declared numerical tolerance on identical inputs, with identical top-10 under fixed tie handling. Cover category routing, left padding, and final-position readout.

Before inspecting further validation results, register one intervention—for example, a fixed uniform/popularity negative-sampling mixture within NextItNet training—and its expected diagnostic effect. Train one replacement checkpoint/category with fixed seeds and budgets; compare once against baseline using unchanged macro validation HR@10, reporting category results and paired user-bootstrap differences. Keep deployment to one checkpoint/category. Training audits generate hypotheses; validation supplies transfer evidence. Log prior validation exposure and stop after this comparison. [Dwork et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/1506.02629) explain adaptive holdout overfitting; this cap limits additional adaptation without undoing earlier selection bias.
